Subject: Private observability — egress & trace connector design review

Hi Mike,

Thanks again for taking time today. As promised, I pulled together a proposed design for how Redwood Private will export logs/metrics/tracing from a VPC/on-prem install into your SIEM and tracing backend with minimal footprint and predictable egress. Please see the attached high-level guide and a diagram (otlp-egress-diagram.png).

Summary of the proposed options (high level):
- Push-based connector running inside customer VPC (Vector/Fluentd) sending to Splunk HEC or S3 (signed uploads)
- Agentless OTLP export for traces using OpenTelemetry collector sidecars -> mTLS to your OTLP endpoint
- Optional syslog/TLS forwarding for legacy devices; buffering to S3 for bulk ingest

Questions for you before we lock this:
1) Which SIEM endpoint do you prefer (Splunk HEC vs S3 landing + ingestion job)?
2) Do you require mutual TLS (mTLS) from the collector/connector?
3) Any strict egress IP allowlist constraints (we can support static NAT or dedicated egress IPs)?

If the answers line up we can schedule a short design review (30 min) w/ your infra and security folks and our infra engineering (Rishi + Lauren).

Proposed next steps: 1) Confirm SIEM endpoint and auth method, 2) Confirm egress packaging (NAT public IP vs VPC peering), 3) Run a small PoC export with sample traces/logs.

Thanks,

Hi all — adding implementation details from the infra/runtime side. TL;DR: we can support both Splunk HEC and S3 fallback with two recommended deployment patterns.

Pattern A — Connector inside customer VPC (recommended for strict allowlists):
- Deploy Vector (or Fluentd) as a set of replicas inside the customer VPC as a DaemonSet / service mesh sidecar — collects app logs and forwards to HEC.
- Outbound egress via a small set of NAT IPs (we can provide recommended CIDR size and help validate).
- Auth: HEC token rotated via Vault agent. Token rotation cadence configurable; connector supports token hot-reload.
- Failover: if HEC is unreachable, buffer to encrypted S3 (SSE-KMS) in the same region then trigger an ingestion job into Splunk.
- Security: require TLS 1.2+, HEC over HTTPS; optional mTLS via client certs (we can produce CSR+cert or accept your CA).

Pattern B — Sidecar OTLP for traces (recommended for low-latency, high-cardinality traces):
- Run OpenTelemetry Collector as a dedicated service, export traces over OTLP/HTTP or gRPC with mTLS to your OTLP endpoint.
- Sampling + tail-based sampling knobs in the collector to limit volume and cost.
- For environments blocking outbound traffic, we can multiplex traces into an S3 buffer and ship on schedule.

Operational considerations:
- Ingress throughput: estimate ~300-700 KBps per 1k concurrent requests; we should run a 48h throughput test to validate quota.
- IAM: use least-privilege roles for S3 uploads; use KMS key restricted to account.
- Egress IPs: we can publish a list of static IPs for NAT egress or configure a VPN peering if your security team prefers private connectivity.
- Trace correlation: we'll include a redwood_instance_id and request_id in all telemetry so you can join logs/traces.

Attached is a sample Splunk HEC payload and a minimal Vector config that demonstrates buffering and HEC failover (splunk-ingest-example.txt).

Happy to run through the PoC steps; if security wants us to avoid public egress we can prototype a direct S3-only pipeline first.

-Rishi

Quick operational points from the Console/ops side:
- Audit and retention: we will emit connector-level audit events to your audit log endpoint and keep a copy in the private deployment for 30 days by default (configurable).
- Dashboards: we can pre-configure a per-customer 'ingest health' dashboard showing buffer utilization, HEC success rate, and last-sync timestamp.
- Rate limiting: provide per-connector rate controls so you can throttle to avoid SIEM quota spikes during incidents.
- Rollouts: we recommend a canary rollout (5% traffic) for the connector and a test run to S3 for verification before enabling HEC.

Operational checklist to include in PoC:
1) Confirm HEC token + rotation frequency
2) Provide egress allowlist or approve NAT ranges
3) Provide a test Splunk index + low-priv ingest token
4) Approve KMS key usage for S3 fallback

I'll own provisioning the dashboard and the canary rollout steps.

-Lauren

Thanks Mike (and security team) — appreciate the quick feedback. Recap / agreed approach:
- Primary ingestion: Splunk HEC over TLS with mTLS (we'll accept client certs)
- Fallback: Encrypted S3 landing (SSE-KMS) with an ingestion job your team controls
- Egress: we'll support static NAT IPs (we will provide a /29 candidate list) or VPN peering if you prefer private connectivity
- Auth: HEC token stored in Vault with automated rotation; certificates can be provisioned via CSR workflow or you can supply a CA
- Ops: Redwood will provide an 'ingest health' dashboard, canary rollout (5%), and audit events streamed to your audit pipeline

Next actions:
- Security: confirm whether you want to supply the CA or have Redwood generate client certs (reply here)
- Mike: please send the test HEC endpoint and a low-priv token or let us know if you prefer S3-only PoC first
- Rishi/Lauren: please prepare a short PoC runbook and one-week availability window (we suggest next Tue/Wed).

I'll set up a 30-minute design/PoC planning meeting for next week once we hear from security. Thanks team.

Best,
Marissa
